messages.content: The influx of South Asian families into mid-tier West End housing typically boosts demand for versatile kitchens and community-oriented spaces, potentially driving modest rental rates upward. From an urban development standpoint, this demographic shift suggests a strategic opportunity to repurpose vacant single-family lots where demolished homes once stood. However, planners must proactively address potential infrastructure strain and ensure zoning reforms accommodate these families' long-term settlement needs.

The assistant responds by analyzing how this demographic shift affects housing demand (kitchens, community spaces) and urban planning requirements (zoning, infrastructure).
